back: A process involving devices and practices that enable an organisation to set performance objectives and to effectively oversee their progressive achievement – a performance steering process.
Management control is the responsibility of managers. The controller supports them in designing and implementing the management system (business partner role).

The dynamics of managing performance in two main phases:
1) planning (upstream of the action)
2) monitoring and analysis of results (downstream)
Results feed back into planning.

front: Two functions of the control cycle
back:
Regulation – update action plans/targets based on results.
Learning – update the qualitative performance dimensions (learning loop).
Performance management carried out locally by the managers in charge of responsibility centres – distinct from control by higher hierarchical levels.
A set of indicators to assess performance for a given purpose. A construct, tailor-made for each organisation.
A measure chosen to monitor achievement of an objective. It allows the objective to be set and the result to be evaluated.
Operational translation of a performance dimension in the form of a type of result to be achieved.

1) Validity with respect to the objective
2) Reliability
3) Ease of implementation
+ principle of relevance

front: Validity with respect to the objective
back: Ability of a measurement to accurately reflect the phenomenon measured or the intention underlying the objective.
Extent to which a measurement can quantify a result with a limited margin of error.
Cost of producing the measurement, its timely delivery and its ease of interpretation.
A measurement can serve multiple uses, so it must be adapted to the specific use for which it is intended → measurement systems are diverse.
Taking the results obtained into account to update action plans or targets set during planning, with a view to improving performance.
Process of updating the qualitative dimensions of performance underlying the measurement system.
Only unfavourable gaps between objectives and results lead to special monitoring. By extension: management intervenes only if the entity's objectives are at risk.
Management reporting informs managers about the performance of parts of the organisation (control purposes). External reporting targets users outside the organisation.
Basis of financial accounting: aggregates the legal entities' statements into consolidated statements (third-party reporting). Contributes marginally to management reporting.

Global: the entity's overall performance. Analytical: sub-groups.
Management accounting → by business segment.
Financial accounting → by legal entity.
A subdivision of an organisation's or responsibility centre's activity (product, market …) that can be evaluated for management decisions (develop, withdraw, allocate resources).
A legal subdivision within a group that must publish statutory financial statements (company accounts).
